add.k: A fire-starting mutant orphan from Scott's old orphanage
st: In season 3, Rusty begs not to go back to his adopter Killgrave, who brainwashes him into a mutant army until Cyclops breaks the hold.
In season 2, Rusty is among the Acolytes at their Savage Land base when the X-Men come for Graydon Creed.

files.notes: Only 'Rusty' is said on screen (no surname, never 'Firefist'), so n is Rusty. Killgrave's brainwashed mutant children are never given a group name, so TAS tm is Independent. The X-Men '97 S2E7 step rests on the Marvel Database (image from that episode, history says he joined Exodus' Acolytes); he is not named or identifiable in that episode's dialogue, so the step and the Acolytes stage are worth a visual check.

add.k: Scott's childhood friend, who now runs his old orphanage
st: In season 3, Sarah, now running her and Scott's old orphanage, helps Cyclops save its children from Killgrave and vows to rebuild.

files.notes: The orphanage is never named in dialogue (the wiki calls it McNeil/McNiel Orphanage), so tm is Independent.

add.k: A Kentucky miner's son who flies with blasting power
st: In season 5, Sam blasts miners free of a cave-in, nearly falls into a secret program's trap, then leaves Cumberland with his family.

files.notes: 'Cannonball' is never said in Hidden Agendas; he is called Sam Guthrie and Samuel Guthrie. The mine and Kirkland's 'Peace Corps' operation are unnamed and he never really serves the latter, so tm is Independent. The Marvel Database also lists a Season 1 Episode 1 on-screen-only cameo (a picture on a monitor), not given a step.

add.k: An Allied captain who sends Logan on a mission in 1944 Paris
st: In season 5, in 1944 Paris, Captain Sawyer sends Logan to free Cocteau from the Chateau du Mort, with Captain America as backup.

files.notes: Named on screen as 'Happy Sawyer' and 'Captain Sawyer' ('Samuel' is never said). His army or unit is never named (Logan says he himself worked for the OSS), so tm is Independent.

add.k: The senator who chairs the plague hearings in Washington
st: In season 2, Senator Goode chairs the plague hearing, cuts off Graydon Creed, calls Beast and clears the chamber in the chaos.

files.notes: No wiki page exists; built from the Time Fugitives transcripts ('Thank you, Senator Goode'; he says 'Security, clear the chamber'). He appears in both parts (both timelines of the hearing), one step. The TV announcer calls it the Senate Committee hearings, so tm uses the app's existing 'U.S. Senate'.

add.k: A village mother in Africa whose son Mjnari is Storm's godson
st: In season 2, Shani tells Storm that her son Mjnari has changed, and recalls how Storm saved him the day he was born.

files.notes: The transcript has Shani say 'This boy is my son' and 'I gave birth to Mjnari, but Storm is the one who breathed life into him'; the batch note's 'Storm's son' reading does not match the dialogue, so she is written as his mother and Storm as godmother. The Marvel Database lists a non-speaking cameo in Sanctuary Part 1 (season 4), not given a step.

add.k: Ka-Zar's wife in the Savage Land
st: In season 2, Shanna is carried off by Sauron to Sinister's citadel, then distracts a guard so Ka-Zar can free the prisoners.

files.notes: Seen unnamed being chased by Sauron in Mojovision (ep 24), named by Ka-Zar in Reunion Part 1, speaks in Reunion Part 2. Non-speaking cameo in Savage Land, Strange Heart Part 2 (season 3) not given a step. Her people are never given a group name, so tm is Independent.

add.k: A Japanese mutant who blazes with solar fire
st: In season 1, Sunfire is forced to build Genosha's dam, and once Gambit frees the slaves' powers, he joins their uprising.
In season 3, Sunfire is among the heroes helping people on Earth as D'Ken unleashes the M'Kraan Crystal.
In season 5, after Xavier is struck down on TV, Sunfire calls for war on humans and rallies behind Magneto on Genosha.

files.notes: Named in Slave Island ('Dry that concrete evenly, Sunfire'); speaking in Slave Island and Graduation Day. Forced slave labour is treated as captivity (as the app does for Storm, Gambit and Jubilee there), so season 1 is Independent; the Genosha stage follows Magneto's Genosha army in Graduation Day. The season 3 step rests on the Marvel Database (a cameo in Phoenix Saga Part V); a monitor-only cameo in Sanctuary Part 1 is not given a step.

add.k: Logan's lost love from his covert-ops past
st: In season 4, Silver Fox, thought dead, admits she sent Logan the photo, then helps him uncover their faked memories and fight Talos.

files.notes: Batch guessed villain because of her Hydra gear, but Hydra is only a logo on her vehicle and costume (never said), so it is not used as her group and she gets a hero file: on screen she works with Logan, Maverick, Sabretooth and Beast. Team X is the app's existing name for the old unit she served in.

add.k: Kisara's hot-headed brother in a Japanese fishing village
st: In season 4, Soichi defies the Silver Samurai's tribute collectors and rallies his village to fight back, with Logan at his side.

files.notes: The batch says Bloodlines, but Soichi, Kisara, Takaki and the Silver Samurai are in The Lotus and the Steel (Wikipedia ep 60, season 4), confirmed by the transcript ('He is my brother, Soichi').

add.k: A flame-wielding Brotherhood mutant with a British manner
st: In season 1, Pyro fights Rogue on Muir Island, then helps stage a diversion at the Capitol in the plot to kill Senator Kelly.
In season 2, Pyro, Avalanche and the Blob loot a market, then attack the X-Men at a hospital as a diversion for Mystique.
In season 2, from a detention cell, Pyro watches Exodus claim the Acolytes' attack on the news and threaten Graydon Creed's life.

files.notes: Named in The Cure ('They call me Pyro'). Season 1 also covers his non-speaking Slave Island cameo. X-Men '97 S2E7: he is not an Acolyte there (itsastampede.com's list of the 31 Acolytes seen leaves him out); the Avalanche (Earth-92131) profile at marvunapp.com puts him in a detainment cell watching Exodus's broadcast, matching the Marvel Database image from that episode. Not named in its dialogue. tm stays The Brotherhood.

add.k: A fiery Shi'ar Imperial Guardsman with a feared temper
st: In season 3, Starbolt fights the Starjammers and the X-Men for D'Ken, then battles the X-Men on the Moon over the Phoenix.
In season 1, Starbolt is among the Imperial Guard who overrun Ronan's Kree soldiers for Deathbird in the war with the Kree.

files.notes: Names himself on screen ('You have angered Starbolt! My rage is feared throughout the empire!'). 'Imperial Guard' is said on screen and matches the app's group file tm. X-Men '97 S1E6: non-speaking; the Ronan and Vulcan (Earth-92131) profiles at marvunapp.com list him among the Guard that routs Ronan's Kree in the opening battle ('Victory for the Imperial Guard!'), matching the Marvel Database image from that episode. Not named in its dialogue.

add.k: A psychic of the Shi'ar Imperial Guard
st: In season 3, Oracle fights for the Imperial Guard against the Starjammers, then battles the X-Men on the Moon over the Phoenix.
In season 4, Oracle warns Lilandra of Deathbird's attack, but Apocalypse carries her off for her power until the X-Men free her.

files.notes: 'Sybil' is never said. Named as Oracle in Dark Phoenix Part IV and Beyond Good and Evil Part 2 (Lilandra: 'I know already, Oracle'; 'my psychics named Oracle'). Raft file because she fights the X-Men across two season 3 arcs; season 4 she is a victim, hence Allied. Her lines are not clear from subtitles, which have no speaker names.

add.k: One of the Silver Samurai's bikers in rural Japan
st: In season 4, Takaki rides with the Silver Samurai's bikers to collect tribute, threatens Soichi, and joins the raid on the village.

files.notes: In The Lotus and the Steel (not Bloodlines, as the batch says). Named once ('No, Takaki. We do not need a martyr.'), apparently by the lead biker when Takaki threatens Soichi; which biker he is, and which lines are his, rests on that line and the wiki. The Samurai's gang is never given a group name, so tm is Independent. Thin case on the name test; drop if the reviewer disagrees.

add.k: A failsafe robot guarding the old Weapon X lab
st: In season 4, Talos, a failsafe robot at the Weapon X ruins, tries to capture Logan's group for reprogramming until they blow it up.

files.notes: A robot, not the Skrull; it announces 'I am Talos'. Destroyed, so Deceased. The program behind it is never named as a group in the dialogue, so tm is Independent. The Marvel Database's Deadly Reunions entry is an unnamed hallucination (S.H.I.V.A.), not given a step.

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Cyclops catches Rusty after a fire at the orphanage and tells him his power takes time to learn. Rusty warns him that Killgrave is bad news, and Cyclops later breaks Killgrave's hold on him.
stages.whoA: The X-Man who believed him at the orphanage
stages.whoB: An orphan he helped free from Killgrave

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Sarah runs the orphanage where Rusty lived and sends him back to Killgrave, not believing his warnings. She then helps Cyclops free Rusty and the other children.
stages.whoA: The woman who runs his orphanage
stages.whoB: An orphan from her home, taken by Killgrave

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Scott returns to his old orphanage and finds his childhood friend Sarah running it. Together they expose Killgrave and save the children, and she offers him a home, but he goes back to the X-Men.
stages.whoA: Her childhood friend from the orphanage, Scott
stages.whoB: His childhood friend who runs the orphanage

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Rogue visits Sam in Kentucky as Ms. LeBeau and learns of Kirkland's offer. She fights Kirkland's troops in his hometown, and Sam thanks her for looking out for him.
stages.whoA: Rogue, who came to look out for him
stages.whoB: A young Kentucky mutant she looked out for

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Xavier and Beast come to Cumberland to find Sam before Kirkland does. Xavier offers him a home at the school, but Sam stays with his family.
stages.whoA: Xavier, who offered him a place at the school
stages.whoB: A young mutant he offered a home

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: In 1944 Paris, Captain Sawyer briefs Logan on rescuing Cocteau from the Chateau du Mort. He tells Logan to call him Captain, not Happy, and pairs him with Captain America.
stages.whoA: Logan, the agent he sent to the chateau
stages.whoB: The captain who sent him to the Chateau du Mort

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Senator Goode chairs the plague hearing and calls Beast to testify. When the attack breaks out in the chamber, he orders security to clear the room.
stages.whoA: The scientist he called to testify
stages.whoB: The senator who called him to testify

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Graydon Creed blames mutants for the plague before Senator Goode's committee. Goode cuts him off and calls Beast to the stand instead.
stages.whoA: An anti-mutant witness he cut off
stages.whoB: The senator who cut him off

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Shani tells Storm her son Mjnari has changed, and recalls how Storm, then living in the village, breathed life into him at birth. Storm drives the Shadow King out of him and brings him back to her.
stages.whoA: Storm, her son's godmother
stages.whoB: The mother of her godson Mjnari

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: The Shadow King takes over Shani's son Mjnari to lure Storm back to the village. Storm and Rogue force him back into the astral plane.
stages.whoA: The being who took over her son
stages.whoB: The mother of the boy he possessed

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Ka-Zar fights to free his wife Shanna, a prisoner in Sinister's citadel. She signals and distracts a guard, and he frees her and the other captives.
stages.whoA: Her husband, Ka-Zar
stages.whoB: His wife, Shanna

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Sauron hunts Shanna down in the Savage Land and carries her off. Ka-Zar later learns she is a prisoner in the citadel.
stages.whoA: The winged creature who carried her off
stages.whoB: A Savage Land woman he carried off

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: On Genosha, Jubilee rallies Sunfire and the other slaves to rush the guards, and the plan fails. Once the collars are off, they fight their way free together.
stages.whoA: The girl who rallied the slaves
stages.whoB: A fellow slave on Genosha

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Sunfire slaves on the Genoshan dam alongside Gambit. Gambit then shuts off the collars, and Sunfire cries out that they can use their powers.
stages.whoA: The Cajun who freed the slaves' powers
stages.whoB: A mutant slave he freed on Genosha

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: After Xavier is attacked, Sunfire calls for war and joins the mutants on Genosha who beg Magneto to lead them. Magneto calls off the attack when he learns Xavier is dying.
stages.whoA: The leader he rallied behind on Genosha
stages.whoB: One of the mutants in his Genosha army

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Silver Fox sends Logan the photo that brings him to the old lab, where they find their memories were faked. He insists their cabin was real, but she says goodbye.
stages.whoA: Logan, the man she loved
stages.whoB: His lost love, Fox

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Silver Fox and Sabretooth, old comrades from the lab, search it for answers with Logan and Maverick. They open the sealed chamber together and fight Talos.
stages.whoA: An old comrade from the lab
stages.whoB: An old comrade, Fox

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Beast finds the lab's video records that explain the faked memories to Silver Fox and the others. He readies the mini jet for their escape.
stages.whoA: Logan's friend, Mr. McCoy
stages.whoB: Logan's old love, Ms. Fox

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Opening the sealed chamber sets off Talos, which tries to capture Silver Fox and the others for reprogramming. They destroy it.
stages.whoA: The robot sent to reprogram her
stages.whoB: One of the subjects it hunted

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Soichi calls Logan a coward for staying out of the fight. Logan then backs him, the village fights the bandits, and Logan beats the Silver Samurai.
stages.whoA: Logan, the gaijin who fought for the village
stages.whoB: The young villager who stood up to the bandits

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Soichi refuses to pay the Silver Samurai's tribute and leads the village against his bandits. The Samurai turns on him until Logan steps in.
stages.whoA: The bandit lord who extorts his village
stages.whoB: The villager who defied him

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Mystique calls Pyro to Muir Island, where his kidnapping of the fake Dr. Adler exposes her. Later he and the Brotherhood act as her diversion in the Kelly plot and at a hospital.
stages.whoA: The shape-shifter he works for
stages.whoB: One of her Brotherhood

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Pyro flirts with Rogue in a Muir Island pub and a fight breaks out, and later she beats him and Avalanche. They clash again at the Capitol, and later she spots his gang looting a market.
stages.whoA: Rogue, who keeps beating him
stages.whoB: A Brotherhood firebug she fights

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Searching Muir Island for Avalanche, Pyro runs into Cable, who is also hunting Dr. Adler. Both go after the scientist for their own ends.
stages.whoA: Cable, his rival for Dr. Adler
stages.whoB: A Brotherhood mutant also after Dr. Adler

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Bishop fights the Brotherhood at the Capitol during the plot against Senator Kelly. He turns Avalanche's power back on them, and Pyro flees.
stages.whoA: The time traveler who drove him off
stages.whoB: A Brotherhood mutant he drove off

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Starbolt is part of the Imperial Guard that D'Ken sends against the Starjammers. The Guard fights for him until he takes the M'Kraan Crystal.
stages.whoA: His emperor, D'Ken
stages.whoB: One of his Imperial Guard

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Empress Lilandra sends the Imperial Guard to fight the X-Men on the Moon for the Phoenix. Starbolt fights in her name.
stages.whoA: His empress, Lilandra
stages.whoB: One of her Imperial Guard

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: On the Moon, Starbolt boasts that his rage is feared across the empire and chases Rogue. She taunts him and slips away.
stages.whoA: Rogue, who taunts him on the Moon
stages.whoB: A hot-headed guardsman she taunted

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Starbolt and Oracle serve together in the Imperial Guard. They fight the Starjammers for D'Ken and the X-Men on the Moon.
stages.whoA: A fellow Imperial Guard
stages.whoB: A fellow Imperial Guard

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Oracle serves in the Imperial Guard that D'Ken sends against the Starjammers and the X-Men. The Guard fights for him until he takes the M'Kraan Crystal.
stages.whoA: Her emperor, D'Ken
stages.whoB: One of his Imperial Guard

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Oracle fights for Lilandra on the Moon and later warns her of Deathbird's attack on the palace. Lilandra then asks Xavier for help when Apocalypse takes Oracle.
stages.whoA: Her empress, Lilandra
stages.whoB: One of her psychics

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Apocalypse helps Deathbird attack Lilandra's palace only to carry off Oracle. He holds her with other psychics to remake time, until the X-Men free them.
stages.whoA: Apocalypse, who abducted her
stages.whoB: A Shi'ar psychic he kidnapped

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Takaki rides with the Silver Samurai's bikers, who collect his tribute from the village. When the village refuses, the Samurai orders it destroyed.
stages.whoA: The bandit lord he rides for
stages.whoB: One of his bikers

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: When Soichi refuses to pay the tribute, Takaki threatens him and is held back. Soichi then leads the village against the bikers' raid.
stages.whoA: The villager who defied him
stages.whoB: A biker who threatened him

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Logan joins the villagers against the Silver Samurai's bikers when they raid. The bandits are beaten and the Samurai is humbled.
stages.whoA: The gaijin who beat his gang
stages.whoB: One of the Samurai's bikers

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Talos wakes when Logan's group opens the sealed chamber and tries to capture them. Logan tears open its back so Maverick can blow it up.
stages.whoA: A Weapon X subject it hunted
stages.whoB: The failsafe robot at the lab

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Talos tries to capture Sabretooth with the others for reprogramming. Sabretooth fights it with a blaster.
stages.whoA: A Weapon X subject it hunted
stages.whoB: The failsafe robot at the lab

stages.title: X-Men: The Animated Series
stages.text: Talos attacks while Beast works to open the lab's doors. Beast helps fight it off.
stages.whoA: Logan's friend, Mr. McCoy
stages.whoB: The failsafe robot at the lab

stages.title: X-Men '97
stages.text: Deathbird leads Starbolt and the Imperial Guard onto Ronan's warship in the war with the Kree. The Guard routs the Kree soldiers while she beats Ronan herself.
stages.whoA: Deathbird, who leads the Guard against the Kree
stages.whoB: One of the Imperial Guard she leads against the Kree

changes.was: ["In season 2, Pyro turns up among the mutants at the Acolytes' Savage Land base when the X-Men come for Graydon Creed.", "X-Men '97", "At large"]
changes.now: ["In season 2, from a detention cell, Pyro watches Exodus claim the Acolytes' attack on the news and threaten Graydon Creed's life.", "X-Men '97", "In custody"]
changes.why: Pyro is on screen in Strange Land, Savage Heart, but not at the Acolytes' base: a fan list of the 31 Acolytes visible in the episode leaves him out and says he appears there in another role, and the Earth-92131 Avalanche profile says Avalanche and Pyro watch Exodus's broadcast from their detainment cells. Kept (on screen, watching the news, as app steps for Mary Jane and the Silver Samurai in X-Men '97 do), corrected, and status set to In custody.

changes.was: ["In season 1, Starbolt serves in the Imperial Guard when Deathbird's followers rise against Xavier at Lilandra's court.", "X-Men '97", "Allied"]
changes.now: ["In season 1, Starbolt is among the Imperial Guard who overrun Ronan's Kree soldiers for Deathbird in the war with the Kree.", "X-Men '97", "Allied"]
changes.why: The sources that place Starbolt in Lifedeath Part 2 put him in the opening battle, where Deathbird leads the Imperial Guard (Earthquake, Flashfire, Gladiator, Manta, Smasher, Starbolt, Titan, Vulcan, Warstar) onto Ronan's warship and the Guard takes down his Kree soldiers. No source puts him at the court fight over Lilandra's engagement. He is on screen fighting, so the step stays, corrected.

The Guard routs the Kree soldiers while she beats Ronan herself.", "whoA": "Deathbird, who leads the Guard against the Kree", "whoB": "One of the Imperial Guard she leads against the Kree", "ep": 6}]}

changes.where: tie Pyro / Anna Marie, stage text
changes.was: Pyro flirts with Rogue in a Muir Island pub and a fight breaks out, and later she beats him and Avalanche. They clash again at the Capitol and at a hospital.
changes.now: Pyro flirts with Rogue in a Muir Island pub and a fight breaks out, and later she beats him and Avalanche. They clash again at the Capitol, and later she spots his gang looting a market.
changes.why: In A Rogue's Tale, Rogue is not in the hospital fight: the trio is 'a mere distraction' while the X-Men search the hospital for Rogue, whom Mystique has led away, and Storm beats them. Rogue only sees Pyro's gang at the farmers market raid ('Old buddies from Muir Island').
